Class 4 · Chapter 5 of 9

Measure and convert units

Read the scale and convert length, mass or capacity before calculating.

  1. See it
  2. Try it
  3. Practise it
  4. Print it
  5. Check it

This chapter works best after Perimeter, area and symmetry. You can still look around, or jump to the check.

By the end I can…

  • I can measure from a non-zero mark.
  • I can combine or share mixed units.
  • I can use balances and temperature scales.

1 See it

Screen 1 of 4

Measure from the right mark

A ribbon may not start at 0. Look at where it begins.

It starts at 3 and ends at 9. The length is 9 − 3 = 6 cm.

Subtract the start from the end.

Screen 2 of 4

Convert, then combine

1 m = 100 cm. 1 kg = 1000 g. 1 l = 1000 ml.

Add 2 m 60 cm and 1 m 45 cm.

That is 3 m 105 cm, so 4 m 5 cm.

Screen 3 of 4

Read the scale

Look at how much each small mark is worth.

Here every tick is 1 degree.

The thermometer reads 23 degrees.

Screen 4 of 4

Balance the crates

Three identical crates weigh 1200 g.

Share 1200 g into 3 equal parts.

One crate weighs 400 g.

Words to know
convert
Change a measurement into a different unit, like metres to centimetres.
mass
How heavy something is. We use grams and kilograms.
capacity
How much a container holds. We use millilitres and litres.

For parents

What your child learns

A level balance means both pans weigh the same. A thermometer reading goes up when it is warmer. When we split something equally, first take away any known amount, then divide what is left by the number of equal shares.

A common slip

Children often add or subtract without converting units. Write everything in the same unit first. After a rise in temperature, add to the reading.

5-minute home activity: Balance and share

  1. Draw a balance with 2 equal crates on one pan and 120 g on the other.
  2. Work out the weight of one crate.
  3. Draw a thermometer reading 22 degrees and mark 11 degrees more.
  4. Share 2200 g into 2 equal parts.
